papers.title: Somnus, a tunable, open-source platform for automated EEG sleep scoring in physiological and disease mouse models
papers.abstract: Many studies using mouse models of human brain disorders rely on extended recordings of brain electrical activity through electroencephalogram, or EEG. The features that researchers measure in these recordings, such as seizures and epileptiform activity, are deeply influenced by whether the animal is awake, in non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep, or in rapid eye movement (REM) sleep. Because total sleep duration varies naturally across animals, rigorous experimental comparisons require classifying the sleep state of every few seconds of a recording. Manual annotation is highly labor-intensive, often requiring hours per subject. While automated scoring tools accelerate this process, they are typically trained exclusively on healthy cohorts and frequently fail when applied to disease models that exhibit atypical or fragmented sleep architecture. Somnus is an open-source Python package designed to automate rodent sleep staging using EEG, muscle activity (EMG), and optional video-tracking data. It includes a robust base model trained on diverse recordings from six independent laboratories, enabling out-of-the-box classification across various equipment setups without requiring prior manual labeling. A central feature of Somnus is its capacity for rapid adaptation to pathological sleep structure. The software provides a graphical interface that directs researchers to the specific epochs where the base model is least certain. Users can manually correct these targeted epochs in a built-in viewer by comparing the model's classification to the raw EEG signal and video, and then use their corrections to fine-tune the model. This workflow empowers researchers to generate accurate custom scorers for complex disease models or novel treatments with just a few minutes of manual correction, bypassing the need to hand-score entire experimental cohorts or develop their own models from scratch.

ai.summary: Somnus is an open-source Python platform for automated sleep staging in rodents using EEG, EMG, and optional video. Its base model, trained across diverse recordings from six laboratories, enables rapid fine-tuning via a graphical interface that targets uncertain epochs, allowing accurate custom scorers for disease models with minimal manual correction.

papers.title: SSSI: A simulation-based framework for evaluating sigma-power fluctuation state identification pipelines in NREM sleep EEG.
papers.abstract: Sigma-band activity of the electroencephalogram during non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep exhibits infraslow fluctuations. These sigma-power fluctuations (SPFs) contain recurring local waveform periods, including ascending, high, descending, and low-sigma-power portions, which can be operationally categorized as SPF states. Although some SPF states are associated with arousal-related processes and sleep fragility, how the prevalence of SPF states changes within a continuous sleep episode remains unknown. Resolving this question requires a reliable analysis pipeline, yet it has been difficult to determine which pipeline best identifies SPF states. Here, we present the Simulation of SPF and SPF-State Identification (SSSI) framework, which generates simulated SPFs with known reference SPF states and uses them to evaluate candidate SPF-state identification pipelines. With a pipeline selected through SSSI, mouse NREM and human N2 sleep showed within-episode changes in SPF-state proportions in both species, with additional age-dependent variation in humans. Pipeline evaluation further showed that the detection of these effects can depend on the pipeline. Together, these findings establish SSSI as a framework for evaluating and interpreting within-episode temporal changes in SPFs while assessing pipeline-dependent methodological bias.

papers.title: Irreversible functional network deformation induced by preprocessing scheme order in multivariate EEG recordings.
papers.abstract: The analysis of Electroencephalographic recordings is non-trivial, the order in which filtering and re-referencing are applied during multivariate signal preprocessing has a critical and underappreciated consequence for functional network estimation. Using EEG sleep recordings from healthy subjects, synthetic data from controlled numerical models (Nf-Tori and IAAFT surrogates), and surrogate-based statistical testing, we provide a quantitative comparison of two preprocessing schemes that differ solely in the order of filtering and re-referencing (filtering followed by re-referencing-FR, and re-referencing followed by filtering-RF). We show that the RF scheme induces spurious cross-correlations that increase systematically with the frequency band and are strongly modulated by the power spectral exponent β of the signal. Critically, for signals with steep power spectra (β ≥2), a regime that characterizes slow-wave sleep, epileptic post-ictal periods, anesthesia, neonatal, and patients in vegetative states, the RF scheme produces artificial correlations that are irreversible. They cannot be eliminated post-hoc even when surrogate-corrected cross-correlations (SAC-matrix) are applied. The mechanism underlying this effect is due to the high-amplitude slow-frequency components that dominate the median reference signal over extended time intervals, embedding redundant information across all channels. In contrast, the FR scheme introduces only small, systematic negative shifts in cross-correlations that are not statistically significant and can be effectively corrected using surrogate-based methods. We therefore recommend the FR scheme combined with surrogate-corrected cross-correlations for all applications involving signals with β ≥2. Although this finding is demonstrated in EEG, it applies to any multivariate recording where spatial re-referencing and band-pass filtering are applied sequentially.

ai.reason: Demonstrates irreversible network artifacts from filtering/re-referencing order, including slow-wave sleep; critical for EEG preprocessing and sleep data reproducibility.
ai.summary: The paper quantitatively compares two EEG preprocessing schemes that differ only in the order of filtering and re-referencing, using sleep EEG, synthetic models, and surrogate testing. It shows that re-referencing followed by filtering induces spurious cross-correlations that increase with frequency band and spectral exponent, becoming irreversible for steep spectra (β ≥ 2), whereas filtering followed by re-referencing introduces only small, correctable negative shifts; the authors recommend filtering followed by re-referencing with surrogate correction for such signals.

papers.title: NESTApp: A GUI-Based MATLAB Application for Auditable TMS-EEG Preprocessing with EEGLAB
papers.abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) preprocessing determines signal quality and interpretation, particularly for transcranial magnetic stimulation combined with EEG (TMS-EEG), where recordings are affected by large and complex stimulation-related artifacts. Several preprocessing approaches have been developed, but substantial variability remains in how pipelines are implemented, documented, and evaluated across recordings, limiting reproducibility and comparability across studies. We developed NESTApp, a MATLAB-based graphical interface built on EEGLAB, to provide an accessible and reproducible framework for implementing and evaluating TMS-EEG preprocessing pipelines. Rather than prescribing a specific pipeline, NESTApp allows users to construct and consistently apply customisable workflows incorporating established EEGLAB and TMS-EEG processing tools, while automatically documenting processing decisions and parameters. Integrated quality-control procedures track data removal and flag recordings based on user-defined criteria, facilitating systematic evaluation across participants. The application also supports group-level visualisation and export of processed TMS-EEG measures for subsequent analyses. Applied to 29 recordings from 16 participants, NESTApp processed 27 and identified those requiring further inspection. By integrating pipeline implementation, documentation, quality control, and group-level evaluation within a single interface, NESTApp provides a transparent framework for TMS-EEG preprocessing that may improve reproducibility, facilitate consistent processing across cohorts, and lower technical barriers to the implementation of established preprocessing approaches.

papers.title: What EEG doesn't see: a whole-brain MEG map of sleep spindles and slow oscillations
papers.abstract: Sleep spindles and slow oscillations (SOs) are hallmarks of non-rapid eye movement (NREM) sleep, linked to memory consolidation and restorative functions. They are usually detected in one or a few scalp electroencephalography (EEG) channels with parameters that vary across studies, and serve as the reference even in magnetoencephalography (MEG), fMRI and intracranial studies. We argue that these choices filter which neural activity is captured. Nineteen young adults took a daytime nap during simultaneous MEG and EEG. Using MEG source imaging across 416 cortical, subcortical and cerebellar regions, we mapped the amplitude and density of SOs (0.5-4 Hz, and 0.5-2 and 2-4 Hz separately) and of spindles (9-18 Hz, and slow, 9-12.9 Hz, and fast, 13-18 Hz, separately), and related each region's activity to a single scalp derivation (Cz-M1). Both rhythms were detected throughout the brain, including the thalamus, hippocampus, amygdala, basal ganglia and cerebellum. The balance between bands varied across regions: fast spindles predominated over slow spindles along the dorsal midline, around the central sulcus and in the thalamus, slow spindles predominated in occipital cortex and the cerebellar hemispheres, and 2-4 Hz SOs were relatively most prominent in occipital cortex. Amplitude and density formed reliable but distinct maps: regions with larger fast spindles also had more of them, whereas SOs, and slow spindles once source depth was controlled, were larger where they were less frequent. More SOs were detected in every region than at Cz-M1, whereas more fast spindles were detected at Cz-M1 than in any single region. Around the SO, slow-spindle activity had the same timing at the scalp and in the sources, but the up-state increase in fast-spindle activity seen at the scalp was absent from local sources. Slow spindles were the most strongly shared events, and sensorimotor sources the most scalp-like. Thus, a single scalp derivation offers a selective and partly composite view of sleep oscillations, with implications for interpreting their functional roles and for targeting them with closed-loop auditory stimulation

papers.title: Predicting ICU Seizures Using 1 hour of cEEG.
papers.abstract: Continuous electroencephalography (cEEG) is the gold standard for detecting electrographic seizures in the intensive care unit (ICU), but limited resources limit prolonged monitoring for all patients. We developed an automated, interpretable pipeline that uses a single hour of cEEG to estimate near-term seizure risk across multiple prediction windows. We retrospectively studied 50 adults who underwent ICU cEEG monitoring at a single tertiary center. From a 1-hour segment, we computed automated interictal-ictal continuum (IIC) burden probabilities for lateralized periodic discharges (LPDs), generalized periodic discharges (GPDs), and lateralized rhythmic delta activity (LRDA), along with quantitative background EEG features reflecting signal organization and hemispheric asymmetry. Segments were labeled by seizure occurrence within the subsequent 1, 2, 4, 8, 12, or 24 hours. Support vector machine (SVM) and bagged-tree classifiers were trained using clinical-only, background-only, and combined feature sets with a 70/30 patient-level train-test split and cross-validation within the training set. For the 4-hour horizon, the combined-feature SVM achieved 76% accuracy and the lowest Brier score (0.25), outperforming clinical-only (72%) and background-only (70%) models. Across horizons, SVM accuracy declined from 94% (1 hour) to 79% (24 hours) with increasing Brier scores, indicating reduced calibration at longer intervals. AUC-receiver operating characteristic increased with wider prediction windows, consistent with higher seizure prevalence at longer lead times. Integrating automated IIC probabilities with quantitative background EEG features enables moderate, interpretable near-term seizure prediction from a single hour of ICU cEEG. Initial external validation on an independent multicenter ICU cohort supports generalizability, although broader prospective and multicenter evaluation are needed before clinical deployment.

papers.title: Visual cues in MI-BCI induce biases in EEG classification models with deep learning but not with standard machine learning.
papers.abstract: Deep learning classification methods are increasingly popular in the brain-computer interface (BCI) field due to their ability to learn complex, non-linear representations from EEG data. Unlike traditional machine learning approaches, which typically rely on hand-crafted features, deep learning models autonomously extract spatio-temporal features directly from the raw or minimally preprocessed signal. However, this flexibility may come at the cost of reduced interpretability and increased susceptibility to confounding factors. This study aims to investigate whether the inclusion of task-related visual cues in the input EEG window biases deep learning models by leading them to exploit irrelevant features, thereby compromising their neurophysiological validity. This study investigates how including EEG signals measured during visual cue presentation on classification accuracy and feature extraction in motor imagery (MI)-based BCIs. Three classification pipelines were evaluated: CSP+LDA, a traditional machine learning approach; DeepConvNet, a convolutional neural network for EEG classification; and REVE, a Transformer-based EEG foundation model. All methods are trained and tested on two large scale open-access EEG datasets using two epoching strategies, with or without including the visual cue onset, to assess their impact on model performance and neurophysiological relevance. Attribution maps (e.g., Saliency maps) and CSP patterns are used to interpret the features learned by each model. Including the visual cue onset significantly improved the classification accuracy of DeepConvNet and REVE. However, attribution analysis showed that the model mainly relied on early parietal activations, most likely cue-related visual evoked potentials, rather than MI-related sensorimotor rhythms (ERD/ERS), which were more prominent when the cue onset was excluded. In contrast, CSP+LDA showed minimal accuracy changes across conditions, with consistent motor cortex activation patterns. These findings demonstrate that higher classification performance does not necessarily imply neurophysiological validity. In particular, deep learning models may exploit confounding signals, such as visual cue processing, which undermines their interpretability and applicability in asynchronous or real-world BCIs, in which there is no such cue. We advocate for systematically applying explainability tools in BCI research to ensure classifiers rely on task-relevant brain activity. Additionally, we emphasize the importance of excluding visual cue periods from EEG segments containing reposenses evoked by the visual cue onset from the input to deep learning models.

papers.title: Distinct electroencephalography alpha-band rhythms map macroscale brain gradients.
papers.abstract: Brain gradients provide a low-dimensional framework for describing cortical organization, linking functional connectivity, anatomy, development, and transcriptional architecture. Whether this macroscale organization also structures fast electrophysiological dynamics remains less clear. Here we used the longstanding observation that alpha-band activity is not unitary, and that some individuals exhibit multiple alpha peaks, as an entry point for examining cortical gradients in resting-state electroencephalography (EEG). We analyzed source-reconstructed EEG from 608 adults, comprising 3,255 recordings acquired across eyes-open and eyes-closed rest before and after cognitive testing. Within individuals, parcel-wise alpha peak frequencies frequently departed from unimodality, revealing 2 separable alpha-frequency components in 38.3% of recordings. These components were not spatially arbitrary: frequency-defined clusters aligned with canonical functional networks, most prominently separating visual and somatomotor systems, although their relative frequency ordering varied across individuals. Low-dimensional analysis of cluster network composition further identified 2 principal axes: a sensory-differentiation axis contrasting visual and somatomotor contributions, and a sensorimotor-association axis resembling established functional-connectomic gradients. These findings suggest that split alpha reflects multiple sensory-anchored oscillatory modes embedded within macroscale cortical gradients, linking a classical EEG phenomenon to the brain's hierarchical architecture.

ai.summary: Using source-reconstructed resting-state EEG from 608 adults (3,255 recordings), the study found that 38.3% of recordings had separable alpha-frequency components that aligned with canonical functional networks, especially separating visual and somatomotor systems. Low-dimensional analysis identified a sensory-differentiation axis and a sensorimotor-association axis resembling functional-connectomic gradients, linking split alpha to macroscale cortical organization.

papers.title: Fixed-Sequence OFF-to-ON Differences in Low-Beta State Dynamics in Parkinson's Disease: A Paired Source-Space Resting-State EEG Study.
papers.abstract: Resting-state EEG studies in Parkinson's disease (PD) have largely emphasized static power or connectivity, whereas fixed-sequence OFF-to-ON session differences may also involve the temporal organization of network states. Paired source-space evidence under such fixed acquisition protocols remains limited. We analyzed 64-channel eyes-closed resting-state EEG in 39 patients with PD contributing paired OFF/ON recordings for the prespecified 90 s primary analysis; 24 also contributed paired 178 s recordings for duration robustness. After individual MRI-based source reconstruction, low-beta (13-20 Hz) dynamic amplitude-envelope connectivity was computed with 2 s windows. Primary endpoints were switching rate (SR) and normalized Shannon entropy (H); fractional occupancy (FO_path) and mean dwell time (MDT_path) of an internally defined OFF-dominant state were prespecified secondary conditional endpoints and are interpreted only as conditional summaries. PD-only linear mixed-effects models quantified the fixed-sequence OFF-to-ON session contrast; medication state and session order were necessarily collinear. In the 90 s analysis, the later ON session showed higher SR (β = 3.3224, Holm p = 0.00406) and H (β = 0.06781, Holm p = 0.000749) than the earlier OFF session. FO_path (β = -0.09167, Holm p = 1.08 × 10⁻⁵) and MDT_path (β = -1.05171, Holm p = 0.00524) were lower in the later ON session. The 178 s reanalysis preserved the same directions, although SR and especially MDT_path were more parameter-sensitive across sensitivity analyses. The fixed OFF-then-ON protocol was associated with reproducible within-subject differences in low-beta state dynamics, with the strongest evidence arising from SR and H. Because medication state was perfectly collinear with session order, these findings cannot distinguish medication-specific effects from order-, time-, vigilance-, fatigue-, or adaptation-related influences. FO_path and MDT_path remain conditional summaries tied to an internally defined OFF-dominant state, and MDT was less stable in the 178 s and OFF-only sensitivity analyses.

The fixed OFF-then-ON protocol confounds medication state with session order, time, vigilance, fatigue, and adaptation, so medication-specific effects cannot be distinguished.

papers.title: Electroencephalographic complexity and cognitive decline: Insights from approximate entropy across aging and dementia.
papers.abstract: Physiological aging involves gradual modifications of brain activity patterns sometimes leading to pathological outcomes. Understanding changes in brain signal complexity from healthy aging to mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and Alzheimer's disease (AD) may provide insights into cognitive decline and support early diagnosis. Electroencephalography (EEG) data were collected from 269 participants divided into three groups: healthy elderly (HE, n = 109), MCI (n = 75), and AD (n = 85). Approximate entropy (ApEn) was computed for the total EEG spectrum and frequency bands. A random forest classifier with a one-versus-one strategy and recursive feature elimination (RFE) was used for group discrimination. Additionally, group comparisons and correlations with neuropsychological scores were performed to further investigate the functional relevance of these entropy changes by assessing their association with cognitive and functional performance. Significant group differences in total ApEn were found, particularly in central brain regions, with progressive decreases from HE to MCI and AD. Frequency-specific patterns emerged: (1) delta ApEn was increased in those with AD across the scalp; (2) alpha 1 ApEn showed frontal decreases and occipital increases in the AD group, with an intermediate pattern in MCI; (3) gamma ApEn was markedly reduced in those with AD compared to both HE and MCI groups, with central and frontal localization, and extended occipital differences in those with MCI versus AD. The classifier achieved 66.55% accuracy, with sensitivities of 78.90% (HE), 49.33% (MCI), and 65.88% (AD). Positive correlations were found between ApEn and cognitive scores in both the total EEG spectrum and gamma band; conversely, delta and alpha 1 ApEn showed negative correlations with cognitive and functional scores. The distinct entropy patterns observed across frequency bands and scalp/brain regions may help characterize electrophysiological changes associated with cognitive decline and AD.

A random forest classifier achieved 66.55% accuracy, with sensitivities of 78.90% (HE), 49.33% (MCI), and 65.88% (AD).

papers.title: An Explainable Self-Supervised Temporal Transformer for Participant-Level Classification of Depressive Symptoms From Resting-State EEG.
papers.abstract: Resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) has emerged as a promising non-invasive modality for investigating depressive symptoms; however, conventional deep-learning methods often require large labeled datasets and provide limited interpretability. We developed an Explainable Self-Supervised Temporal Transformer Network for participant-level classification of BDI-defined elevated depressive symptoms from resting-state EEG. The framework employed masked temporal modeling for self-supervised pretraining followed by supervised fine-tuning. Model performance was evaluated using repeated nested participant-wise cross-validation and compared with conventional machine-learning and deep-learning baselines. Explainability was investigated through transformer attention maps and SHAP-based channel attribution. The proposed model achieved a receiver operating characteristic area under the curve (ROC-AUC) of 0.82 (95% CI: 0.73-0.90), a precision-recall AUC of 0.69, balanced accuracy of 0.75, sensitivity of 0.72, and specificity of 0.78. The positive predictive value was 0.57, indicating a substantial false-positive burden in the evaluated cohort. The proposed model showed the highest point-estimate ROC-AUC among the evaluated baselines, with a 0.07 improvement over EEGNet; however, the overlapping uncertainty intervals and the small elevated-symptom cohort warrant cautious interpretation of comparative superiority. Performance decreased from an ROC-AUC of 0.82 in Run 1 to 0.78 in Run 2 and to 0.72-0.73 under cross-condition transfer, supporting interpretation of these analyses as internal reproducibility and condition-shift assessments rather than independent external validation. Removing self-supervised pretraining reduced the ROC-AUC to 0.74. Explainability analyses identified distributed temporally relevant intervals and frontal-midline to centro-parietal channel contributions, with attribution interpreted as model-relevance evidence rather than causal biomarker evidence. Overall, the findings provide preliminary internal evidence that self-supervised temporal representation learning can support participant-level classification of BDI-defined elevated depressive symptoms from resting-state EEG under the evaluated experimental conditions. The findings do not establish clinical diagnostic validity, screening readiness, or independent external generalizability.

papers.title: Attenuated alpha state transitions and disrupted repetition-dependent temporal adaptation in mild cognitive impairment
papers.abstract: Mild cognitive impairment (MCI) may involve impaired dynamic regulation of brain states that is not captured by conventional resting-state electroencephalography (EEG). We quantified occipital alpha (8-12 Hz) transitions during three repeated eye-opening/eye-closure cycles in 60 healthy controls (HC) and 77 participants with MCI. Eye-state events were refined from frontal ocular artifacts. Transition magnitude was measured by the log-transformed post-/pre-event energy ratio, and transition success by the expected direction of alpha change. For canonical transitions meeting prespecified fit-quality criteria, mono-exponential fitting yielded transition onset (t_onset) and the post-onset time constant (tau). MCI showed weaker alpha suppression during eye opening, weaker alpha enhancement during eye closure, and lower odds of transition success. No significant group difference in tau was detected within the canonical quality-controlled subset. In contrast, t_onset showed significant Group x Trial interactions in both conditions: HC developed later onset during eye opening and earlier onset during eye closure across repetitions, whereas MCI showed no comparable change. These findings suggest reduced alpha state-transition capacity and altered repetition-dependent temporal organization in MCI.

ai.reason: Quantifies alpha transition dynamics and adaptation across repeated events; relevant to state-space/time-series modeling and event-related spectral analysis, with moderate transfer to vigilance-state tracking.
ai.summary: In 77 participants with mild cognitive impairment and 60 healthy controls, occipital alpha (8-12 Hz) transitions during repeated eye-opening/eye-closure cycles were weaker and less successful in MCI, with no group difference in post-onset time constant. MCI showed absent repetition-dependent temporal adaptation: healthy controls developed later onset during eye opening and earlier onset during eye closure across trials, whereas MCI did not.

papers.title: Selective Auditory Attention Decoding with a Two-Node Wireless EEG Sensor Network
papers.abstract: Objective. Selective auditory attention decoding (sAAD) enables neuro-steered hearing devices by identifying the attended speaker in a multi-speaker environment from neural activity recorded with electroencephalography (EEG). Despite algorithmic progress, practical deployment remains constrained by a lack of wearable, unobtrusive, and fully wireless EEG acquisition solutions. We therefore evaluate whether reliable sAAD can be achieved under the realistic hardware constraints of a wireless EEG sensor network (WESN) of miniaturized, galvanically isolated EEG sensor nodes. Approach. We use a WESN of two synchronized, compact around-ear EEG sensor nodes worn bilaterally. Each node provides four local EEG channels derived from five pre-gelled electrodes, including a local reference. Sample-wise wireless synchronization of data from both nodes enables joint processing as an eight-channel EEG. On a newly recorded dataset, we apply correlation-based stimulus decoding, followed by hidden Markov model (HMM)-based post-processing. Main results. Stimulus decoding achieves an average sAAD accuracy of 69.24% on 60s decision windows, comparable to previously reported wired around-ear EEG systems that measure long-distance scalp potentials. HMM-based post-processing further improves this to a steady-state accuracy of 77.17% with an average simulated attention switch detection time of 32.79s. Combining sensor nodes at both ears outperforms single-ear configurations, primarily through redundancy rather than complementary spatial information. Finally, a fixed bipolar configuration using four electrodes per ear, yielding three channels, suffices to maintain performance. Significance. These results demonstrate the practical feasibility of sAAD using a fully wireless, galvanically isolated around-ear WESN and establish a realistic performance benchmark under practical hardware constraints.

ai.summary: Evaluated selective auditory attention decoding using a two-node wireless around-ear EEG sensor network and achieved 69.24% accuracy on 60s windows, improving to 77.17% steady-state with HMM post-processing and 32.79s attention switch detection time.

papers.title: Robust and replicable effects of ageing on resting-state brain electrophysiology measured with MEG.
papers.abstract: Non-invasive recordings of brain electrophysiology provide credible insights into decline in neuronal functioning with age. New approaches are required to translate these results into compelling clinical metrics and meet the global challenge of preserving brain health in ageing. Changes in neuronal dynamics with ageing are observable in the power spectra of EEG and MEG recordings. Highly promising candidates for electrophysiological markers have been identified, but progress is hindered by substantial methodological variability across studies. This makes it challenging to establish a clear consensus on the frequency, location, and direction of any single reported effect within the larger body of research. We estimate a full-frequency whole-head profile of the ageing effect on eyes-closed resting-state MEG using the GLM-Spectrum. This data representation is easily sharable, facilitates meta-analyses, and provides a framework for estimating statistical power of age effects for future study planning. We use this to show that the effect of age replicates across open-access MEG datasets and is robust to modelling of common covariates. Distinct components within the full-frequency profile have different effect sizes, indicating that sample-size planning for ageing effects must consider the specific features of interest. The frequency profile of ageing is strongly robust to a range of common covariates and partially robust to modelling of grey matter volume. We establish that what seems a well-powered study may become underpowered when analyses target an age effect that is linearly separable from an age-relevant covariate such as grey matter volume. These results provide a pathway towards formal comparison and assessment of candidate markers for brain health in ageing.

papers.title: An EEG-based framework for Alzheimer's disease diagnosis via single-channel multi-entropy fusion and ensemble learning.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer's Disease (AD) is a prevalent neurodegenerative disorder characterized by progressive cognitive decline, and its early diagnosis is vital for timely intervention. However, most existing EEG-based diagnostic methods rely on multi-channel devices confined to hospital settings, limiting their accessibility for community screening. To address this gap, this study aims to develop a lightweight processing approach for portable, low-cost devices to support early AD diagnosis using single-channel EEG data, integrating signal purification with complementary entropy-based feature extraction and ensemble learning. Specifically, EEG signals are first decomposed into five brain rhythms (δ, θ, α, β, γ) using Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT). Empirical Mode Decomposition (EMD) is then applied to extract Intrinsic Mode Functions (IMFs) from the selected rhythm. Four entropy measures, including Differential Entropy (DE), Singular Spectral Entropy (SSE), Fuzzy Entropy (FE), and Sample Entropy (SE), are subsequently extracted from each IMF to construct the Multi-IMF Entropy Matrix (MIMFEM). After that, an ensemble learning framework combining five classifiers is designed to discriminate AD patients from healthy controls (HCs). The proposed method is evaluated on two public datasets using Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation (LOOCV). Using single-channel EEG data, our approach achieves classification accuracies of 97.92% on the Florida-based dataset and 81.54% on the AHEPA dataset, with corresponding F1-scores of 97.87% and 82.86%, respectively. These results, achieved with limited data sources, show that our approach provides an effective, practical solution for single-channel wearable AD screening and addresses the critical need for low-cost, accessible early diagnostic tools, advancing Artificial Intelligence (AI) in healthcare through a lightweight model.

papers.title: MTDANet: lightweight multi-scale temporal hierarchy and distance-regularized linear attention network for motor imagery brain-computer interfaces.
papers.abstract: Motor-imagery (MI) electroencephalography (EEG) offers a non-invasive route to brain-computer interaction, yet reliable single-trial decoding remains difficult because task-related patterns are weak, nonstationary, and distributed over multiple temporal scales. This study investigates whether a staged local-to-global model can integrate fine temporal-spatial structure with longer-range context without relying on unrestricted self-attention. We propose MTDANet, an architecture that combines multi-scale temporal-spatial feature extraction, factorized temporal consolidation, and distance-regularized recurrent attention. The model was evaluated on three public MI datasets under subject-specific and leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) protocols. Separately initialized models were also trained on P300 and steady-state visual evoked potential (SSVEP) datasets to examine broader architectural applicability. Participant-level paired analyses used two-sided paired t tests with within-setting Holm correction. MTDANet achieved subject-specific accuracies of 85.61 ± 8.32%, 90.85 ± 7.62%, and 87.79 ± 13.93% on BCI Competition IV 2a, BCI Competition IV 2b, and BNCI2014_002, respectively. Relative to the highest-mean baseline, the paired improvements were supported after within-setting Holm correction on BCI Competition IV 2a (3.56 percentage points, adjusted p = 0.0097) and 2b (1.62 points, adjusted p = 0.0168). Under LOSO evaluation, the corresponding accuracies were 63.31 ± 15.74%, 79.77 ± 7.57%, and 79.96 ± 11.95%. The 2.08-point BNCI2014_002 difference had a 95% confidence interval of 0.42-3.73 points and an adjusted p value of 0.0387. These three comparisons did not remain significant in a broader 56-comparison Holm sensitivity analysis. The P300 and SSVEP models attained the highest observed mean accuracies. The results provide within-setting evidence for staged local-to-global temporal modeling in offline MI-EEG evaluations.

papers.title: AOR: adaptive orthogonal regression for depression feature selection with incomplete EEG channels.
papers.abstract: Depression induces severe mental and physical impairments, highlighting theclinical need for rapid and reliable detection. Electroencephalography (EEG) directly reflectsneural electrical activity and serves as a promising tool for depression investigation. However,the inherent non-stationarity, redundancy, and noise susceptibility of EEG signals, togetherwith the common issue of incomplete channel data due to electrode loss or severe noise duringacquisition, compromise the reliability of diagnostic models. Existing EEG feature selectionmethods lack adaptability to such incomplete data, leading to distorted feature evaluation anddegraded performance. To address this limitation, an adaptive orthogonal regression(AOR) method is proposed for EEG feature selection for depression detection under incompletechannel conditions. The method integrates three core innovations: embedding missing channelinformation into the orthogonal regression formulation to mitigate the impact of incompletechannels, incorporating adaptive channel-weighted learning to automatically quantify therelative importance of different channels, and applying global redundancy minimizationto eliminate inter-feature redundancy while enhancing discriminability. The optimizationproblem is solved via Generalized Power Iteration and Augmented Lagrangian Multipliermethods. AOR was validated on the MODMA and PRED-d003 datasets across3-channel, 64-channel, and 128-channel configurations under single-modal and multi-modalscenarios. Experimental results demonstrate that AOR consistently outperforms state-of-the art methods across various missing ratios and channel configurations. The average cross-subjectdepression recognition accuracy reaches 92.25 % and 95.12 % across different missing ratios onthe two datasets. Additionally, feature weight analysis reveals that EEG kurtosis consistentlyexhibits high discriminative power across different configurations. The proposedAOR method provides a robust and efficient solution for depression feature selection underincomplete EEG channel conditions, offering reliable diagnostic performance in real-worldclinical scenarios.

papers.title: Decoding object categories from electroencephalography during free viewing reveals early information evolution compared to passive viewing.
papers.abstract: Object processing is central to visual perception, and its neural substrates inform cognitive and computational models of vision. Electroencephalographic (EEG) research has increasingly adopted multivariate pattern analysis (MVPA) to decode distributed neural representations, moving beyond average signal changes and predefined electrodes. Yet, most MVPA studies use passive viewing paradigms that constrain eye movements and evoke brain activity by external stimuli presentation, creating an artificial dissociation between perception and action. Here, we examine object category representations during active vision by combining MVPA with a deconvolution method for overlapping fixation-related responses. By decoding category information from single fixations, we compare the temporal dynamics of object processing between free viewing (active) and rapid serial visual presentation (passive) conditions. We find that categorical information, across multiple levels of abstraction, can be decoded from individual fixations during natural viewing, and that object representations generalize across passive and active conditions. Notably, representational dynamics time-locked to fixation onset emerge earlier than those time-locked to stimulus onset. We discuss the possibility that object processing begins parafoveally, aligned with saccade onset, rather than foveally at fixation. Thus, information about what and when to expect new information, available in free viewing, facilitates processing. These findings underscore the importance of studying vision in naturalistic settings and highlight key methodological considerations for combining MVPA with deconvolution in overlapping neural data. Object processing is fundamental to visual perception and to cognitive and computational models of vision. Although MVPA has advanced EEG research by enabling the decoding of distributed neural representations with high temporal precision, it has been applied primarily in passive viewing paradigms that constrain natural eye movements. The current study bridges the gap between passive and active vision research by combining MVPA with overlap deconvolution to decode object category information from EEG during natural fixations in free viewing. This approach reveals that category-specific representations emerge earlier in active viewing, likely reflecting processing that begins during saccade planning or execution. The findings underscore the importance of studying vision under ecologically valid conditions and introduce a novel methodological framework for capturing neural dynamics during active perception.

papers.title: Hypoxia Disrupts Multiple Processes Supporting Spatial Navigation
papers.abstract: Hypoxia impairs cognitive function, yet its effects on navigation and intrinsic brain activity remain poorly understood. This study investigated whether a continuous exposure to hypoxia (CH) or an intermittent exposure to hypoxia (IH) differentially influence navigation performance and resting-state electroencephalography (EEG) in healthy young adults. Seventy-two participants completed sham (FiO2 = .209) and hypoxia (FiO2 = .13) sessions during either a one hour of CH or IH intervention. Navigation was assessed using the Spatial Performance Assessment for Cognitive Evaluation (SPACE), while resting-state EEG was recorded before and after the intervention in a subset of participants (n = 40). EEG spectra were parameterised into periodic (alpha and beta power and central frequency) and aperiodic (exponent and offset) components. Aligned rank transform (ART) analyses of variance examined effects of hypoxia and intervention group, while linear regression determined whether reductions in peripheral oxygen saturation (SpO2) predicted changes in navigation or EEG. Hypoxia impaired multiple components of navigation, increasing path integration distance error and egocentric pointing angle error irrespective of intervention group, while mapping accuracy was preferentially impaired following IH and perspective taking performance following CH. Hypoxia also reduced alpha and beta power, beta central frequency, and aperiodic exponent, while aperiodic offset and alpha central frequency remained stable. The reduction in aperiodic exponent was primarily evident following IH, suggesting that the temporal pattern of oxygen delivery may influence specific neurophysiological responses. Contrary to our hypothesis, SpO2 reduction did not predict individual differences in navigation performance or EEG activity. These findings demonstrate that brief, moderate hypoxic exposure can disrupt allocentric and egocentric components of spatial navigation while selectively altering periodic and aperiodic features of intrinsic brain activity.

papers.title: GROND: Automated characterization of periodic and rhythmic EEG patterns.
papers.abstract: Periodic discharges (PDs) and rhythmic delta activity (RDA) are common EEG patterns in critically ill patients that require characterization of lateralization, spatial localization, and frequency. Manual characterization is subjective and time-consuming. We present an automated system for all four major subtypes: lateralized and generalized PDs (LPD, GPD) and lateralized and generalized RDA (LRDA, GRDA).Approach. The PD-Profiler combines a per-channel convolutional neural network, hemisphere-specific learned evidence traces, dynamic programming with an approximately periodic prior, and discharge-locked topographic localization. The RDA-Profiler uses iterative narrowband Hilbert refinement for frequency and lateralization, with phase-locking-value analysis for spatial extent. Both pipelines were trained and evaluated on 12,425 EEG segments from 11,729 patients.Main results. Four electroencephalographers independently scored 200 stratified segments per subtype. The algorithm exceeded expert-expert (EE) agreement on LPD frequency (expert-algorithm (EA) ICC 0.931 versus EE 0.897; p<0.001) and was statistically indistinguishable from EE on GPD frequency (EA 0.980 versus EE 0.973; p=0.061), GRDA frequency (p=0.056), LRDA frequency (p=0.435), LPD laterality (EA kappa 0.945 versus EE 0.974; p=0.079), and LRDA laterality (EA kappa 0.961 versus EE 0.993; p=0.269). No attribute fell significantly below the EE ceiling. PD discharge timing achieved an F1 of 0.817 at single-sample precision (mean absolute timing error 3.1 ms). PD spatial localization reached 97.3% of expert inter-rater Jaccard agreement, and RDA spatial extent matched EE agreement.Significance. GROND reaches expert-level reliability across lateralization, spatial localization, discharge timing, and frequency for PDs and RDA. In discordant cases, experts judged its frequency estimates more accurate than the original labels in 94% of cases, supporting reproducible characterization at scale.

papers.title: Long-term functional outcome after post-anoxic brain injury: model development and internal validation from a multicentre cohort.
papers.abstract: To identify biomarkers of long-term functional recovery after cardiac arrest (CA). This is a prospective longitudinal cohort study based on the Veneto Registry of CA (July 2021- June 2023). We collected demographic, clinical, biochemical, and electroencephalography and short- and middle-latencysomatosensory-evoked-potentials (S-SSEP and ML-SSEP) within 72 hours. Functional scales were collected at discharge, 3, 6, and 12 months after the event. Multiple imputation was used to avoid statistical loss. Calibration was verified. A penalised logistic regression and a penalised continuation ratio were fitted to model the effect of covariates. The quality of prediction or fitting was verified computing the rank probability score for ordinal outcomes, the Brier score, and area under the ROC curve for binary outcomes. Decision curve analysis confirmed clinical utility. We included 160 persons (mean 62.80 ± SD 14.36 years; 123 males) out of 186. The interaction between continuous/nearly continuous EEG and N20/P25 predictor of survival (β = 0.840) and recovery (β = 1.160) of consciousness at 12 months after CA. ML-SSEP was a predictor of good outcome on all scales at 12 months after CA (0.739<β <1.708). ML-SSEPs associated with standard neurophysiological assessments are robust predictors of long-term functional outcomes after CA. ML-SSEPs associated with EEG and standard SSEP might be incorporated in routine clinical practice in ICU post-anoxic coma assessment.

papers.title: Acoustic Context Shapes Cortical Encoding of Spectral Discrimination in Normal and Impaired Hearing
papers.abstract: The auditory change complex (ACC) provides a cortical measure of acoustic discrimination, yet the mechanisms shaping responses to spectrotemporally complex sounds remain poorly understood. We investigated how acoustic context and temporal-envelope variability influence cortical encoding of spectral contrast in normal-hearing (NH) and hearing-impaired (HI) listeners. Electroencephalography (EEG) was used to record ACCs and auditory steady-state responses (ASSRs) evoked by spectrotemporally modulated stimuli. We compared conventional spectro-temporal modulations (STMs) with a novel discrete spectro-temporal modulation (DSTM) paradigm, examined temporal roving, and evaluated cortical responses to spectral contrast in NH and HI listeners. ACCs elicited by DSTM stimuli were larger and more symmetrical across transition directions than those elicited by conventional STMs. Temporal roving markedly reduced responses to intensity changes while largely preserving responses to spectral changes, indicating a partial dissociation between intensity-driven and spectrally driven cortical discrimination. ACC responses decreased systematically with spectral contrast and were weaker and delayed in HI listeners. By contrast, ASSRs remained highly detectable and showed no systematic dependence on spectral contrast, supporting a distinction between contrast-sensitive cortical discrimination and ongoing envelope encoding. Temporal roving further enhanced separation between NH and HI listeners. ACC response strength was significantly associated with behavioural STM discrimination thresholds and explained variance beyond age and audiometric thresholds. These findings demonstrate that cortical representations of spectral discrimination are shaped by acoustic context and temporal-envelope statistics. Temporal roving attenuates intensity-driven responses while preserving spectrally driven discrimination, providing insight into cortical encoding of spectrotemporal contrast and its relationship to perceptual performance.

papers.title: Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) in schizophrenia: enhancing transparency in clinical decision-making.
papers.abstract: Schizophrenia is a chronic and severe psychiatric disorder affecting nearly 1% of the global population, characterized by positive symptoms such as hallucinations and delusions, negative symptoms including avolition and affective flattening, and cognitive impairments that compromise social and occupational functioning. Despite advances in psychiatry, diagnosis remains largely symptom-based, relying on criteria from the Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM-5) and the International Classification of Diseases (ICD-11), highlighting the need for objective biomarkers and improved clinical decision support. Neuroimaging modalities, including structural and functional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI/fMRI), diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), positron emission tomography (PET), as well as electrophysiological techniques such as electroencephalography (EEG) and magnetoencephalography (MEG), have revealed abnormalities in brain connectivity, dopaminergic signaling, sensory processing, and network dysfunction associated with schizophrenia. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning (ML), have enabled prediction of diagnosis, treatment response, and relapse risk using multimodal clinical, neuroimaging, and genetic data. However, the "black-box" nature of many AI models limits transparency, interpretability, and clinician trust, restricting translation into practice. Explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) addresses these challenges by providing interpretable, transparent, and clinically accountable models that support decision-making while preserving ethical and regulatory standards. By integrating explainable models with multimodal data, clinicians can use them as an adjunct for precision psychiatry, facilitating biomarker discovery, personalized treatment strategies, and trustworthy, actionable decisions, ultimately enhancing transparency and improving outcomes in schizophrenia care.

papers.title: How aging reshapes implicit learning: behavioral and oscillatory evidence from an EEG-adapted Fast Mapping paradigm.
papers.abstract: Most of everyday memory formation occurs without deliberate intent, yet the neural mechanisms supporting implicit encoding and their reorganization with age remain poorly understood. The present study investigated age-related changes in implicit learning using an EEG-adapted Fast Mapping paradigm (the Disjunctive Inference Implicit Learning Test, DIILT) in 31 younger and 35 older adults, paired with a comprehensive neuropsychological assessment and a one-month delayed recognition measure. Behaviorally, younger adults rapidly acquired novel implicit associations across the learning phase, whereas older adults showed persistent reliance on familiar items and limited improvement for novel associations. Critically, both groups successfully retained novel associations after one month, with implicitly learned associations showing greater long-term stability than explicitly encoded ones regardless of age. At the neural level, younger adults exhibited early posterior theta engagement for novel compared to familiar items, which disappeared by the end of learning, consistent with novelty-driven associative encoding. Older adults showed no such theta modulation for novel items, pointing to reorganization of the neural mechanisms supporting implicit encoding. Theta dynamics predicted immediate recognition in younger adults but not in older adults who rather showed theta association with processing speed, suggesting an age-related shift from memory-specific binding to domain-general cognitive resource allocation, consistent with neural maintenance frameworks of cognitive aging. These findings demonstrate that implicit encoding produces durable memory traces across the lifespan but relies on reorganized oscillatory dynamics in aging, with implications for understanding how cognitive aging reshapes everyday memory formation.

papers.title: Chronic Electrophysiology Captures Progressive Variability in DNA-Damaged Cardiac Networks
papers.abstract: Electrophysiological recordings provide a key functional readout of cardiac health. Most in vitro studies rely on acute measurements rather than recording evolving functional changes. Here, we implement a microelectrode array (MEA) based system for chronic electrophysiological monitoring of human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocyte (iPSC-CM) monolayers. Electrophysiology recordings were maintained for up to 40 days, enabling longitudinal assessment of field potential amplitude, field potential duration, beat frequency, conduction velocity, and waveform morphology. Untreated iPSC-CM monolayers exhibited stable electrophysiological behavior throughout chronic culture. Following exposure to the cardiotoxic chemotherapeutic doxorubicin, chronic recordings captured progressive deterioration in electrical activity, including reduced field potential amplitude, altered repolarization dynamics, increased beat-to-beat variability, and reduced conduction that persisted after drug removal. Electrode-resolved analyses further revealed pronounced progressive spatial variability, highlighting localized responses that would be obscured by population-averaged measurements. Endpoint assays indicated reduced calcium transient amplitude and altered calcium reuptake, decreased mitochondrial membrane potential, and loss of connexin 43, findings consistent with the impaired electrical activity observed in chronic recordings. Together, these results establish chronic electrophysiological monitoring as a powerful approach for resolving the spatiotemporal progression of cardiotoxicity and other dynamic cardiac processes in vitro.

papers.title: Motor effort biases perceptual decisions through later-stage evidence accumulation rather than early sensory-attentional processing
papers.abstract: Motor effort has been shown to bias perceptual decisions toward less effortful choices, but it remains unknown whether this bias already takes effect during the early stages of decision formation through preparatory attentional allocation or sensory processing, or during later-stage evidence accumulation preceding response execution. This study investigated when motor effort becomes integrated into decision formation by focusing on the temporal evolution of neural processing during perceptual decision-making. While 64-channel EEG was recorded, twenty-four healthy adults performed an orientation discrimination task in which two Gabor patches appeared simultaneously in the left and right visual hemifield and decisions were reported using two pressure-sensitive response buttons requiring different levels of force. We found that motor effort modulated EEG activity at both the preparatory and later decision stages: pre-stimulus alpha power was reduced over the occipito-parietal cortex contralateral to the low-effort option, and mean centro-parietal positivity (CPP) amplitude preceding response execution was greater over centro-parietal cortex for low-effort choices, while leaving early sensory representations intact as indicated by no differences in P1 or N1 amplitude following stimulus onset. Trial-by-trial CPP amplitude preceding response execution increased with the likelihood of selecting the low-effort option, whereas the pre-stimulus alpha modulation was not associated with behavioral decision bias. These findings suggest that motor effort biases perceptual decisions primarily during later-stage evidence accumulation, thereby providing insight into the neural basis of embodied perceptual decision making.

papers.title: How do Uncompensated Micro-Shifts Systematically Confound Low-Concentration Metabolite Quantification in 1H-MRS Analysis?
papers.abstract: Linear combination model fitting is widely used for spectral analysis in 1H-MRS but relies on basis sets with fixed spin-system parameters, implicitly neglecting the sensitivity of chemical shifts to physiological and pathological tissue microenvironments. This study systematically evaluated the impact of frequency perturbations on spectral analysis and reassessed the validity of the Cramér-Rao lower bounds (CRLB) as a quality-control metric for low-concentration metabolites. The effects of frequency perturbations on spectral analysis were investigated using simulated datasets with different baseline models and lineshapes, followed by validation in a publicly available in vivo human brain 1H-MRS dataset (n = 31). Estimated metabolite concentrations, relative concentration changes, estimation errors, and CRLB values were analyzed across all conditions. Frequency perturbations produced minimal quantification changes in high-concentration metabolites but substantially larger errors in several low-concentration metabolites. Across both simulations and in vivo validation, relative concentration changes generally remained below 3% for high-concentration metabolites but exceeded 10%-20% for several low-concentration metabolites, including Gln, GSH, Asp, and NAAG. Importantly, substantial estimation errors frequently occurred despite CRLB values remaining within conventionally acceptable ranges. These findings were consistently observed across different baseline models, lineshapes, and in vivo validation. Physiologically relevant frequency perturbations can introduce substantial quantification bias that is not consistently reflected by CRLB. These findings identify environmentally induced resonance-frequency variations as an underrecognized source of quantification error in current linear-combination model fitting and suggest that CRLB alone is insufficient for assessing quantification reliability, particularly under conditions associated with altered brain temperature or tissue pH.

papers.title: Toddler EEG power reflects behavioral social engagement state during naturalistic parent-child interaction.
papers.abstract: Social engagement is a critical process for children's language and social development and is altered in neurodevelopmental conditions such as autism. Although previous EEG studies have investigated correlates of children's social development in closely controlled experimental studies, few studies have examined how the brain reflects meaningful behavioral states, such as social engagement, within naturalistic parent-child interaction. This study collected EEG from typically developing toddlers of varying language ability and their parent (n = 49, 24-44 months) during the Social EEG paradigm; dyads completed contexts of dyadic interaction (book reading and puzzle play) and baseline (movie watching) during EEG recording. Videos of the interaction session were coded for social engagement using moment-by-moment behavioral coding and applied to the EEG data. As predicted, child EEG alpha power decreased (p < .001) and theta power increased (p = .01) during social engagement relative to baseline movie engagement. Further, the same pattern was replicated in an independent sample (n = 24, 25-47 months) including children diagnosed with autism, who showed the same pattern of power. These results demonstrate for the first time that EEG power is associated with naturally occurring moments of parent-child social engagement across a range of social/linguistic abilities and ages. This opens avenues for study of more naturalistic and meaningful developmental constructs.

papers.title: Large-scale all-optical electrophysiology links excitability and connectivity to circuit dynamics in vivo
papers.abstract: To understand neural computations, one would like to relate circuit dynamics to neuronal intrinsic excitability and connectivity. We developed tools for large-scale all-optical electrophysiology and applied them to approximately 300 layer 1 interneurons per mouse in vivo. Across two mice, targeted stimulation and voltage imaging identified 1,469 inhibitory and 5,752 directed electrical connections among 14,312 tested pairs. Presynaptic identity was more strongly associated with inhibitory post-synaptic potential (IPSP) amplitude, whereas postsynaptic identity was more strongly associated with IPSP decay time. Gap junctional and synaptic interactions had distinct spatiotemporal kernels, with corresponding signatures in spontaneous activity. Excitability measured under optogenetic stimulus predicted spiking responses to subthreshold voltage, depolarization rate, and spike history during spontaneous firing. Genetic subtypes also showed different behavioral-state-dependent voltage-to-spike relationships despite similar population-average subthreshold voltages. These measurements link cellular properties and pairwise interactions to spontaneous circuit dynamics, establishing an approach for functional circuit mapping in vivo.

papers.title: Electrophysiological signature of stroke recovery: investigating EEG biomarkers for prognostic insights.
papers.abstract: Stroke is a leading cause of long-term disability, often resulting in persistent motor impairments that reflect disruptions in large-scale brain networks. An integrated framework capturing spatiotemporal EEG dynamics would help clarify how these networks change during recovery. We analysed resting-state EEG from stroke patients at 1 week (Session 1) and three months (Session 2) post-stroke to investigate electrophysiological biomarkers of motor recovery, indexed by change in the Fugl-Meyer scale (ΔFM). We quantified relative alpha-band power, microstate metrics (mean duration, complexity, and transition probabilities), and measures of metastability and synchrony derived from the Kuramoto Order Parameter. Change in relative alpha power emerged as the strongest single correlate of motor improvement, accounting for the largest proportion of variance among the EEG measures examined. Metastability and synchrony did not individually reach statistical significance but showed moderate positive correlations with ΔFM, particularly in the alpha and theta bands, and added 26% explained variance in ΔFM when combined with alpha power. Microstate parameters did not explain additional variance once alpha power and network-level dynamics were accounted for. A hierarchical model combining alpha power, metastability/synchrony, and microstates explained over 78% of the variance in ΔFM. These findings indicate that stroke recovery involves restoring balanced alpha oscillations and flexible large-scale brain coordination. Larger samples and more frequent longitudinal assessments are required to confirm the prognostic utility of integrated EEG biomarkers for guiding personalised stroke rehabilitation strategies.

papers.title: Neurite Complexity and Plasticity Markers Track Synaptic Vesicle Density in the Living Human Brain: A Multimodal PET-MRI-EEG Study
papers.abstract: Neuroplasticity, the brain's capacity to reorganise its structure and function, is a transdiagnostic feature across psychiatric and neurodegenerative diseases and a putative mechanism of action for pharmacological interventions. [11C]-UCBJ positron emission tomography (PET), which quantifies synaptic vesicle glycoprotein 2A (SV2A) density, offers the most direct in vivo measure of human synaptic density, but its relationship to complementary, more scalable neuroimaging measures of structural and functional plasticity remains uncharacterised. We combined [11C]-UCBJ PET, diffusion weighted imaging (DWI/NODDI), resting-state functional magnetic resonance imaging (rs-fMRI), and electroencephalography (EEG)-based sensory tasks (roving mismatch negativity, MMN; visual long-term potentiation, vLTP) in 18 healthy volunteers to test the relationship between synaptic terminal SV2A density and complementary structural and functional neuroplasticity measures, and whether these relationships were reproducible following pharmacological challenge with ketamine (n = 11) or N,N-dimethyltryptamine (DMT; n = 7). There were no statistically significant differences in PET-derived SV2A binding potential (BPND), DWI-derived neurite orientation dispersion (ODI) and structural weighted degree (SWD), EEG-derived MMN repetition suppression, and late-phase vLTP P2 potentiation, 1 to 8 days following DMT and ketamine exposure compared to baseline. BPND was coupled with ODI across cortical regions before and after pharmacological challenge, and this relationship was tighter within visual, attentional, and frontoparietal control brain networks. SWD showed a weaker, more spatially restricted association with BPND, primarily in regions belonging to the limbic and visual brain networks, but was not replicated post-drug. No consistent association was found between BPND and functional weighted degree (FWD), derived from rs-fMRI, at baseline or after pharmacological challenge. Frontotemporal BPND was positively associated with MMN repetition suppression (r = 0.61), and occipital BPND with late-phase vLTP P2 potentiation (r = 0.54), with the MMN-BPND association replicating after pharmacological challenge (r = 0.49). These findings link synaptic terminal SV2A density in the living human brain to neurite architecture and the capacity for short-term and Hebbian-like long-term synaptic plasticity, while dissociating these relationships from generic functional connectivity and magnitude of sensory-evoked responses. These data provide cross-modal validation for DWI- and EEG-derived measures as biological indices and surrogate measures of human synaptic plasticity.

papers.title: EEG-Derived Pain Threshold Index-Guided Remifentanil Titration During Laparoscopic Abdominal Surgery: A Randomized Trial.
papers.abstract: To determine whether remifentanil titration guided by the pain threshold index (PTi), an electroencephalography-derived proxy for nociceptive tolerance rather than subjective pain, reduces intraoperative remifentanil infusion during laparoscopic abdominal surgery. In this prospective, single-center, assessor-blinded randomized trial, adults undergoing elective laparoscopic abdominal surgery with propofol-remifentanil target-controlled infusion were assigned 1:1 to PTi-guided or conventional hemodynamic-guided remifentanil titration. The primary endpoint was intraoperative remifentanil infusion rate. The principal analysis used the full-analysis set and covariate-adjusted linear regression with heteroskedasticity-consistent robust standard errors. Among 200 randomized patients, 195 were analyzed (98 PTi-guided; 97 control). The primary endpoint was neutral: mean (SD) remifentanil infusion rate was 7.44 (1.43) versus 7.63 (1.41) µg kg-1 h-1; adjusted mean difference, -0.06 µg kg-1 h-1 (95% CI, -0.44 to 0.32; P=0.758). Per-protocol results were similar. Median (IQR) NRS at post-anesthesia care unit (PACU) admission was 2.0 (2.0-3.0) versus 3.0 (2.0-4.0), and Ramsay score was 2.0 (2.0-2.0) in both groups. In exploratory secondary analyses, rescue opioid was used in the PACU by 18/98 (18.4%) versus 31/97 (32.0%) patients and any rescue opioid through 48 h by 29/98 (29.6%) versus 44/97 (45.4%). Any postoperative nausea and vomiting (PONV) through 48 h occurred in 17/98 (17.3%) versus 29/97 (29.9%) patients. Total postoperative opioid exposure through 48 h was not reduced. PTi-guided remifentanil titration did not reduce intraoperative remifentanil infusion. PACU pain and sedation scores were not materially different. Lower early rescue-opioid use and fewer PONV events through 48 h were exploratory secondary findings, were not accompanied by lower postoperative opioid dose, and require prospective confirmation.

papers.title: Cathodal transcranial direct current stimulation in pediatric epileptic syndromes: mechanisms, limitations, and future research horizons.
papers.abstract: Drug-resistant epilepsy affects approximately 20 to 30% of children with epilepsy, with particularly devastating outcomes in developmental and epileptic encephalopathies (DEEs). Cathodal transcranial direct current stimulation (c-tDCS) has emerged as a promising noninvasive neuromodulation approach warranting systematic evaluation. Recent meta-analyses of randomized controlled trials demonstrate significant reductions in seizure frequency following c-tDCS compared with sham stimulation, corresponding to roughly 3 to 4 fewer seizures per month or a proportional reduction of about 45% at 4 weeks. Evidence supports efficacy in focal epilepsies and selected syndromes, including Lennox-Gastaut syndrome and early-onset epileptic encephalopathies. Standard protocols employ 1 to 2 mA cathodal stimulation for 20 minutes over 5 to 10 consecutive sessions. High-definition tDCS configurations allow more focal current delivery. However, significant inter-individual variability exists, and the relationship between interictal epileptiform discharge suppression and clinical seizure outcomes remains inconsistent. Computational modeling demonstrates substantially higher cortical electric field strengths in children than in adults at equivalent current intensities, raising important dosing considerations. Safety data from over 600 pediatric sessions indicate favorable tolerability with no serious adverse events, although seizure exacerbation has been reported in a minority of participants in open-label studies. Cathodal tDCS represents a safe, tolerable, and potentially effective adjunct to unchanged antiseizure medication regimens in children with drug-resistant focal epilepsy and should presently be regarded as investigational. Selection criteria, optimal stimulation parameters, and syndrome-specific protocols require further refinement. Particular caution is warranted with transcranial alternating current stimulation in generalized epilepsies. Research priorities include closed-loop electroencephalography (EEG)-triggered stimulation systems, biomarker- driven patient selection, age-appropriate dosimetry informed by computational modeling, and adequately powered trials in specific DEE populations including West syndrome, Dravet syndrome, and epileptic encephalopathy with spike-wave activation during sleep.

papers.title: Clinical and Electrophysiological Characteristics of Peripheral Neuropathy in Immune-Related Adverse Event of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitors: A Retrospective Study and Literature Review.
papers.abstract: To summarize clinical and laboratory characteristics of peripheral neurological immune-related adverse event (irAEs-PN) patients, to improve understanding and provide reference for early diagnosis of irAEs-PN caused by immune checkpoint inhibitors. We screened 61 patients with irAEs in our center from September 2020 to June 2025. In addition, studies with detailed clinical data related to irAEs-PN were collected in PubMed database from January 2015 to June 2025. A total of 50 patients with irAEs-PN were included, including 8 cases from our center and 42 cases reported in literature. The patients' demographic information, clinical characteristics, electrophysiological examination, therapy and outcomes were retrospectively analyzed and summarized. Among the eight patients in our center, the first symptom was paresthesia, occurring in two cases, and limb weakness, occurring in six cases. Electrophysiology identified two axonal neuropathies, three demyelinating, and three mixed axonal and demyelinating neuropathies. Among the 42 patients reported in literature, the first symptom was paresthesia, occurring in 39 cases, and limb weakness, occurring in 41 cases. Electromyography identified 13 axonal neuropathies, 25 demyelinating neuropathies, and 4 mixed axonal and demyelinating neuropathies. In most patients, irAEs-PN is characterized by demyelinating sensorimotor involvement of both the upper and lower limbs. In individuals receiving immune checkpoint inhibitors, prompt electromyography after the onset of neuropathic symptoms can aid in detecting neurological involvement and facilitate earlier treatment.

papers.title: Attenuated attention engagement and sensorimotor resonance to social events in first-episode adolescent depression: Evidence from EEG oscillations.
papers.abstract: Depressive symptoms may disrupt social brain development during adolescence, resulting in adverse long-term quality of life. Yet, little is known regarding the cognitive and neural changes during the processing of social interactions in adolescents with first-episode depression, particularly from an allocentric perspective. We used electroencephalography (EEG) to assess two neural indicators during the observation of others' interactions, including sensorimotor mu suppression and occipital alpha-band activity, in 22 adolescents with first-episode major depressive disorder (MDD) and 23 healthy counterparts. Participants observed animated motions wherein actions were directed toward animate (human-like) or inanimate (rock) targets, comprising social (giving) and kinematically matched control events (disposing, taking and acquiring). Healthy controls (HCs) exhibited stronger central-parietal mu suppression in the lower sub-band during observation of socially interactive giving events than disposing events. In contrast, adolescents with MDD manifested no corresponding difference in mu suppression. Additionally, depressive adolescents demonstrated significantly higher occipital alpha power when viewing social (patient) than non-social (rock) targets, and this alpha power was significantly higher than that observed in HCs. Exploratory correlation analyses revealed that attenuated sensorimotor resonance of social interactions was significantly associated with increased severity of depressive symptoms in the MDD group. Adolescents with first-episode depression showed difficulties in efficiently encoding social information and implicitly extracting the social-relational meaning of observed social interactions. These findings critically extend current understanding of neurocognitive mechanisms underlying social cognitive alterations in this population, and provide potential avenues for early screening and targeted interventions of social functioning impairment in adolescence.

papers.title: Sustained Seizure Freedom After Stereo-Electroencephalography Without Definitive Intervention: Evidence for Network Modulation by Invasive EEG.
papers.abstract: Stereo-electroencephalography (sEEG) is a diagnostic technique used to localize seizure-onset networks in drug-resistant epilepsy, typically guiding resection, ablation, or neuromodulation. Sustained seizure freedom after diagnostic implantation alone is rarely described. We describe two patients who achieved long-term remission after sEEG monitoring without definitive surgical intervention. A 39-year-old man with posttraumatic right hemispheric epilepsy underwent implantation of 11 depth electrodes, during which no habitual seizures were captured despite medication withdrawal and provocation. After electrode explantation, he discontinued all antiseizure medications and has remained seizure-free for 71 months. A 63-year-old woman with left temporal epilepsy underwent implantation of 12 depth electrodes; monitoring again failed to capture habitual seizures, although abundant mesial temporal interictal discharges were recorded. After explantation, which was complicated by a small tract hemorrhage, she has remained seizure-free for 20 months on stable cenobamate therapy. These cases add to a limited body of evidence suggesting that sEEG implantation may induce microlesional or network-modulatory effects capable of interrupting seizure propagation, analogous to remission reported after intracranial electrode placement in prior series. Recognition of this phenomenon is clinically important. When no habitual seizures are recorded and early postoperative improvement is observed, a period of extended follow-up may be warranted before pursuing resection, ablation, or neuromodulation. Further study is needed to define predictors of remission, clarify underlying mechanisms, and guide patient counseling regarding this uncommon but meaningful effect of invasive EEG.

papers.title: Stress recovery and restorative effects of viewing different types of peony garden landscapes: a preliminary experiment.
papers.abstract: Substantial evidence supports the health benefits of urban green spaces, yet most studies focus on general landscapes, leaving a gap regarding specialized gardens with topographic variations (flatland, tableland, mountain land). This study explored the restorative effects of peony garden scenes with different topographic characteristics on students' physical and mental health using virtual reality (VR) and the Trier Social Stress Test (TSST). Participants (N = 56 per group, 23 ± 1.5 years old) were exposed to flatland peony garden (FPG), terraced peony garden (TPG), mountainous peony garden (MPG), or indoor environment (IE). Physiological factors were examined using heart rate (HR), heart rate variability (HRV), and electroencephalogram (EEG). psychological evaluation was carried out using the Profile of Mood States (POMS) and State-Trait Anxiety Inventory (STAI). Perceived Restorativeness Scale (PRS) was used to assess subjective perceived recovery. Results showed that: (1) After TSST, HR, LF/HF, and Beta significantly increased (p < 0.01), while R-R, HF, and Alpha decreased (p < 0.01); (2) Compared to the stress stage, viewing FPG, TPG, and MPG led to significant physiological changes (p < 0.05), increased positive emotion (V-A, p < 0.01), and decreased negative emotions (A-H, F-I, T-A, C-B, D-D, anxiety, p < 0.01); (3) Perceived recovery was associated with emotional states, reflected in greater feelings of "being away" and "fascination." The most pronounced changes occurred in the MPG. In the current VR experiment, peony garden landscapes, especially those with abundant landscape elements and visual experience, exhibited therapeutic potential for short-term stress recovery compared with the windowless indoor office scene. The findings offer preliminary guidance for creating health-promoting peony garden landscapes.
