papers.title: 5-HT1A Antagonist WAY-100635 Prevents Chronic Neurodegeneration and Immune Activation After TBI
papers.abstract: Traumatic brain injury (TBI) initiates secondary neurodegeneration that compromises interconnected neural circuits and contributes to persistent visual and neurobehavioral impairment. Pharmacological strategies that preserve vulnerable neurons and synapses while limiting chronic neuroinflammation remain an unmet therapeutic need. We previously identified the serotonin 1A receptor (5-HT1A) antagonist WAY-100635 through screening human stem cell-derived retinal ganglion cells (RGCs) and demonstrated that it promotes neuroprotection through cyclic adenosine monophosphate-dependent mitochondrial biogenesis. Here, we investigated whether post-injury treatment extends this neuroprotective efficacy to cerebral and visual circuitry following TBI. Male C57BL/6J mice aged 2-3 months underwent unilateral controlled cortical impact (CCI) involving the left visual cortex. Mice were randomly assigned to sham, untreated injury or treated injury groups, with 3-10 sham controls and 5-8 mice per injury group across experiments. WAY-100635 was administered intraperitoneally at 5 mg/kg daily, beginning 1 hour after injury and continuing for 6 weeks. Therapeutic efficacy was assessed using motor and psychological-health-relevant risk-taking/behavioral disinhibition by elevated-plus-maze assessment, visual electrophysiology, optokinetic responses, diffusion magnetic resonance imaging, and retinal and cortical histopathology. Unilateral cortical injury produced bilateral RGC dysfunction and loss, with greater degeneration in the eye contralateral to the injured hemisphere, consistent with predominantly crossed murine visual projections. WAY-100635 significantly preserved RGC survival and function, improved visual acuity and contrast sensitivity, and preserved visually evoked cortical responses to contralateral eye stimulation. Diffusion MRI revealed bilateral visual pathway abnormalities, with treatment selectively normalizing fractional anisotropy and radial kurtosis in the optic tract ipsilateral to cortical injury. In perilesional cortex, treatment preserved neuronal cell bodies and synapses detected by synaptophysin immunoreactivity while markedly reducing microglial/macrophage activation and reactive astrogliosis. These effects were accompanied by improved early motor performance and attenuation of injury-associated increases in open-arm exploration in the elevated plus maze. Cortical cavity volume was not significantly reduced, supporting preferential protection of vulnerable circuitry surrounding and connected to the primary lesion. These findings identify post-injury WAY-100635 treatment as a novel therapeutic intervention that combines neuronal and synaptic preservation with reduced chronic glial activation and improved functional outcomes. They support further translational development of serotonin 1A receptor antagonism to limit secondary neurodegeneration and the visual and neurobehavioral consequences of TBI.

Treatment did not significantly reduce cortical cavity volume, indicating preferential protection of perilesional and connected circuitry.

papers.title: Optimal Sound-Color Matching Scheme of Five-Element Music and Lighting Colors for Emotional Responses in Patients with GAD: A Randomized, Two-Factor Mixed-Design Trial.
papers.abstract: Sound-color matching offers a novel approach to enhance music therapy, but the optimal combinations for emotional dysregulation in generalized anxiety disorder (GAD) remain untested. To identify the optimal sound-color matching scheme for emotional responses in GAD patients using Five-Element music and different lighting colors. A randomized two-factor mixed-design trial was conducted between June 2024 and February 2025 at Grade-A tertiary hospitals. Lighting color (cyan, red, yellow, white, black) was the between-subjects variable, and musical emotional valence (positive, neutral, negative) was the within-subjects variable. 210 eligible GAD patients were randomly assigned to five lighting color groups. The audiovisual stimulation combined calibrated LED lighting and validated Five-Element music segments in a standardized laboratory environment. Primary outcomes were subjective valence and arousal scores (Self-Assessment Manikin). Secondary outcomes included skin conductance (SC), skin temperature (ST), heart rate (HR), and electroencephalography (EEG) power spectral density (PSD). All 210 patients were included in the subjective data analysis, with 205 providing valid physiological data and 204 yielding EEG data. Significant interactions between lighting color and music valence were observed for valence scores (F=2.02, p<0.050), arousal scores (F=2.77, p<0.050), ST (F=51.18, p<0.050), and HR (F=39.77, p<0.050). Cyan lighting with positive music produced the highest valence scores (7.79±0.81) and optimal physiological regulation (lowest HR: -15.44±1.89 beats per minute (bpm); highest ST: 0.84±0.09°C). Red lighting with positive music induced the highest arousal (6.83±1.23). EEG analysis revealed a significant interaction only in the theta band (F=1.98, P=0.024), with positive music showing lower PSD across all bands. Among the tested pairings, positive Five-Element music with cyan lighting elicited the most favorable immediate emotional and physiological responses in patients with GAD, supporting further investigation of sound‑color matching as a multimodal adjunctive strategy for emotional regulation. This clinical trial was registered at the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (clinical trial number: ChiCTR2400079878).

papers.title: A Pilot Study of Photon Counting CT Spectral Analysis Following Pancreatic Adenocarcinoma Resection to Differentiate Local Recurrence From Postsurgical Fibrosis.
papers.abstract: To assess photon counting CT (PCCT) spectral parameters in the differentiation of locally recurrent pancreatic adenocarcinoma (PDAC) from benign postsurgical fibrosis after PDAC surgical resection. Twenty-two patients [12 male, mean±SD: age 71 (8) y] who underwent pancreas protocol PCCT following surgery for PDAC were retrospectively identified. Local recurrence required tissue histopathology or enlarging FDG-avid soft tissue. Nonrecurrence required soft-tissue reduction with stable or decreased CA 19-9. Two blinded radiologists independently drew regions of interest within the surgical bed soft tissue to determine iodine density (I), I normalized to aortic enhancement (I%), fat fraction, and extracellular volume (ECV), which were compared using the Mann-Whitney U test. A P<0.05 indicated statistical significance. The intraclass correlation coefficient was used to assess inter-reader reliability. ROC analysis was performed using mean measurements. On pancreatic parenchymal phase imaging, median [IQR] postcontrast attenuation for patients with nonrecurrence (n=10) and recurrence (n=11) was 32.3 (16.4 to 42.9 HU) and 57.0 (50.2 to 65.5 HU)(P=0.001); enhancement was 23.7 (10.2 to 26.0 HU) and 40.0 (34.4 to 44.5 HU) (P=0.001); I was 0.6 (0.5 to 0.90 mg/mL) and 1.8 (1.5 to 2.0 mg/mL) (P<0.001); I% was 8.3 (6.3% to 11.1%) and 34.3 (29.8% to 40.9%) (P<0.001); and ECV was 5.8 (4.4 to 6.9 mL) and 23.0 (18.0 to 25.8 mL) (P<0.001), respectively. To differentiate nonrecurrent from recurrent soft tissue, a postcontrast 45.7 HU threshold had 100% sensitivity and 80% specificity [AUC=0.92 (0.80-1.00)]; enhancement of 31.9 HU had 81.8% sensitivity and 100% specificity [AUC=0.98 (0.93-1.00)]; 14.0 mL ECV had 100% sensitivity and 100% specificity [AUC=1.00 (1.00-1.00)]; 1.27 mg/mL I had 90.9% sensitivity and 100% specificity [AUC=0.99 (0.98-1.00)]; and 20.3% I% had 100% sensitivity and 100% specificity (AUC=1.00). Inter-reader agreement was near-perfect (ICCs 0.86 to 0.96). PCCT spectral parameters demonstrated excellent diagnostic performance in differentiating locally recurrent PDAC from postsurgical fibrosis on pancreatic parenchymal phase imaging.
